text: io- dide does not demonstrate antifungal activity in vitro. Oral itraconazole 200 mg daily for 3 to 6 months is also effective1-3 and is regarded by some3,4 as the treatment of choice. The dose of itraconazole may be increased to 200 mg twice daily in non-responders; alternatively pa- tients may be given oral terbinafine or a saturated potassi- um iodide solution taken orally. Oral fluconazole should only be used in patients who cannot tolerate any of the pre- ferred drugs.4 For patients with osteoarticular infections, oral itracona- zole 200 mg twice daily for at least 12 months is recom- mended, with either liposomal or conventional amphoter- icin B given intravenously as alternatives. Oral itraconazole 200 mg twice daily may be given as mainte- nance therapy once the patient has responded to the am- photericin B treatment.4 Patients with life-threatening pulmonary, disseminated, or meningeal disease should receive treatment for at least 12 months. The drug of choice is intravenous liposomal am- photericin B with conventional amphotericin B given in- travenously as an alternative. Oral itraconazole 200 mg twice daily may be given as maintenance therapy. Oral itraconazole may be given in non-life-threatening pulmo- nary infections and for patients who cannot tolerate am- photericin B.4 Lifelong maintenance therapy with oral itraconazole 200 mg daily may be beneficial after initial treatment for meningeal or disseminated sporotrichosis in immunocom- promised patients, including those with AIDS, if immuno- suppression cannot be reversed.4 1.
